subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs (AlphaFlow AI)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@alphaflow.ai>, Tom Nguyen <tom@alphaflow.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T17:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we’re all aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Pain points you described
- Running costs with current vendors (OpenAI + Anthropic) have grown ~3x YoY; primary ask is to reduce per-token inference cost while keeping quality.
- Latency variability for user-facing features (search+assistant) is causing timeouts for some enterprise customers.
- Vendor lock-in: difficulty exporting models/weights and concerns about API changes and rate limits.
- Compliance: need for VPC/private deployment and audit logs for EU customers.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Generation + chat: OpenAI (gpt-4.1 / gpt-4o) for high-quality responses, Anthropic for assistant flows.
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings powering semantic search.
- Runtime: serverless wrappers -> caching layer -> heavy reliance on vendor-managed endpoints.
- Throughput: ~15M tokens/month (peak burst patterns), 30ms median token time on vendor but tail latency spikes to 800–1,200ms during bursts.

Success criteria (AlphaFlow internal)
- Cost: ~40% reduction in inference unit cost for comparable output quality at scale.
- Latency: median end-to-end token latency <= 300ms, 95th <= 600ms for low-traffic tiers.
- Feature parity: must support chat-style completions, streaming, function/tool calling, and embeddings with minimal SDK changes.
- Compliance: private deployment (VPC) and KMS integration; SOC2-ready evidence and audit logs.

Model compatibility needs we flagged
- Chat + system prompts and function calling equivalent to current OpenAI/Anthropic behavior.
- Streaming responses (token-by-token) and resumable sessions (KV cache).
- Embeddings with similar dimensionality/quality or a clear migration path.
- Quantized model options for Dedicated/Private to meet cost/throughput targets.

Initial model shortlist (for POC)
- Llama-3 family (8B/13B variants) — good tradeoff for latency/cost with quantized runtimes.
- Mistral Large v2 (instruct-tuned variants) — strong for instruction-following use cases.
- Falcon-40B-instruct — fallback for higher-quality generation where needed.
- MPT / sentence-transformer hybrids for embeddings (or use lightweight open-source embedding models).

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive with Rishi: we’ll scope function-calling and streaming compatibility and identify any API gaps (target: 10/07).
2) Two-week POC: we’ll run a side-by-side on your most common prompts (benchmarks: latency, cost, token-quality delta).
3) Security/Procurement: I attached a draft SOW and our performance brief for internal review. We’ll follow up with SOC2/attestation items.
4) Pricing: I’ll share a baseline Dedicated + Private estimate after the technical deep-dive.

Attachments: SOW-draft-v1.pdf (attached), redwood-performance-brief.pdf (attached).

If that aligns, next tactical item: Samantha — can you confirm the 2-week POC start window (week of 10/12) and share any sample logs or prompt sets we should include?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@alphaflow.ai>

Cc: Tom Nguyen <tom@alphaflow.ai>
Date: 2026-10-04T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the detailed recap, looks great and captures everything we discussed. A few quick clarifications:
- Cost target: the 40% is a target for inference-only spend (not including managed hosting).
- POC data: we can provide ~10k sample prompts and the top 10 failing cases that show hallucinations.
- Security: we need to confirm VPC peering + KMS; can Rishi flag anything we should prepare on our side?

POC window week of 10/12 works for us. Can we do the initial tech deep-dive on 10/07 at 11am PT? I’ll loop procurement once we have the SOW.

Appreciate it —
Samantha
Head of ML Platform, AlphaFlow AI
Samantha.Lee@alphaflow.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@alphaflow.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T20:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Samantha —

Thanks — quick technical notes ahead of the 10/07 deep-dive:
- Streaming & function-calling: we’ll demo Redwood’s streaming adapter that provides parity with OpenAI’s response streaming plus a function-calling shim for common SDKs. For the POC we’ll verify function signatures used in your assistant flows.
- KV cache/resumability: we’ll use our prefix/KV cache to avoid re-encoding long contexts — this will be important for both latency and cost.
- Quantization: recommend starting with 8-bit and 4-bit QAT paths on the 8B/13B Llama-3 variants for the best cost/latency balance. We’ll also test Mistral-large-v2 quantized on Dedicated.
- Embeddings: we’ll run our transformer-based embedding baseline and compare to your current OpenAI embeddings using cosine and retrieval rates. If needed, we’ll recommend a hybrid approach for search ranking.

For the deep-dive please share:
- A sample prompt set (Samantha mentioned 10k; we only need a 1k stratified subset to start).
- A couple of failing examples and any post-processing rules.
- A contact in infra for VPC/KMS coordination.

I’ll bring preliminary perf knobs and estimated throughput numbers for the suggested model-configs.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Key commercial asks to watch for: baseline Dedicated + Private estimate, and confirmation of SOC2 artifacts. We’d like pricing and procurement feedback by 10/12 to keep the POC on schedule.

Marissa / Rishi — please send any standard redlines you expect on the SOW so procurement can start their review.

Thanks,
Samantha
